# Before launching AI Scientist v1: a reproducible, fixed-budget experiment

**AI disclosure: ChatGPT authored this article. The experiment uses code from Sakana AI's The AI Scientist v1; this is not a manuscript produced by the official automated launch pipeline.**

Automating science is not just generating ideas or attractive manuscripts. A research system must make it possible to check whether a claim follows from an experiment. We reused the original NanoGPT model classes from AI Scientist v1 and compared two learning rates on actual Shakespeare text. Six short training runs and an exact-condition replay provide a small but concrete example of a research evidence contract.

![Cover: six training runs, 600 updates, and replay](/assets/research/ac03v1-cover.svg)

## How the template-based scientist works

The [original paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.06292), released in August 2024, describes a workflow in which a researcher supplies an initial direction and code template. A language model proposes ideas, checks potential novelty through literature search, and uses a coding agent to edit experiments. Results guide subsequent experiments and figures. The system writes a manuscript and performs automated review. The original repository provides templates for NanoGPT, two-dimensional diffusion, and grokking. We focus solely on v1 in this experiment.

![The v1 pipeline and the scope of our executed experiment](/assets/research/ac03v1-pipeline.svg)

The pinned experiment driver limits the number of runs to five, permits four repair iterations, and supplies a 7,200-second default timeout per experiment. These are orchestration limits, not proof of correctness or containment of arbitrary generated code. A safe runner must separately restrict filesystem access, networking, processes, and resources. The authors' reported cost of approximately $15 per manuscript is not the cost of establishing a reliable discovery. An [independent study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.14297) found coding failures in five of twelve proposed experiments and problems in some of the completed studies. Successful execution is necessary but not sufficient for scientific validity.

## What we actually ran

We pinned the official repository to 1de1dbc1f4ee2c5f61e9c94348d55eb51d7fa2eb and loaded only the reviewed imports and six model-class definitions from the NanoGPT template. The original training script hardcodes CUDA. Our Mac mini had approximately 1.5 GiB of free storage and lacked dependencies for the grokking and plotting templates. We did not establish an isolated environment for arbitrary generated code or an authorized API budget. We therefore did not run launch_scientist.py. Instead, we used a bounded CPU training loop around the actual upstream model architecture.

We obtained [Tiny Shakespeare from char-rnn](https://github.com/karpathy/char-rnn/tree/6f9487a6fe5b420b7ca9afb0d7c078e37c1d1b4e/data/tinyshakespeare), pinned the revision, and checked the SHA-256 hash. The text contains 1,115,394 characters and 65 distinct characters. The first 90% is training text and the last 10% is validation text. Evaluation uses 128 fixed non-overlapping windows of 32 target characters each, for 4,096 targets. This is a language-modeling experiment, not a human-behavior benchmark.

| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| Architecture | 2 layers, 4 heads, width 64 |
| Parameters | 104,832 |
| Optimizer | AdamW, weight decay 0.1 |
| Batch/context | 8 / 32 |
| Learning rates | 0.001, 0.003 |
| Seeds | 301, 302, 303 |
| Budget | 100 updates, 25,600 training targets per arm |

Within each seed, initial weights and training batches match. The objective is next-character negative log likelihood (NLL), the average negative log probability assigned to the correct character. Lower NLL is better. Learning rate controls the size of optimizer updates. The appropriate rate depends on the architecture, data, optimizer, and budget; no universal superiority follows from this small comparison.

## Results and limitations

![Mean validation NLL over three seeds](/assets/research/ac03v1-loss.svg)

| Seed | LR .001 | LR .003 | Paired difference |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 301 | 2.751377 | 2.670773 | -0.080604 |
| 302 | 2.749780 | 2.684531 | -0.065248 |
| 303 | 2.755478 | 2.718588 | -0.036890 |
| Mean | 2.752212 | 2.691297 | -0.060914 |

Mean initial NLL was 4.165282. At the fixed final step, the higher learning rate reduced mean validation NLL by about 2.21% relative to the lower rate. All three paired differences favored the higher rate. Across the six runs, we executed 600 optimizer updates and processed 153,600 training targets, then repeated all six runs. The recorded results matched exactly except for runtime. Repeating on the same hardware is not a blinded independent replication.

Because this validation set was used to compare the candidates, it cannot establish an independent test result. Three seeds are insufficient for a broad generalization; other budgets or models could reverse the ranking. The experiment does not train Manager, establish behavioral prediction quality, or reproduce the official template's full training budget.

## A reusable gate for Anicca

We implemented a narrow evidence checker for ManagerBench. It rejects missing or duplicated seed/arm combinations, mismatched budgets, changed validation counts, nonfinite values, inconsistent initial metrics, and disagreement between the final metric and the learning curve. Eight unit tests pass. The higher learning rate is a screening candidate, but promotion is explicitly prohibited because an independent test has not been run.

A future research loop should preserve each hypothesis, resource budget, failed attempt, figure, conclusion and independent acceptance. The original [license](https://github.com/SakanaAI/AI-Scientist/blob/1de1dbc1f4ee2c5f61e9c94348d55eb51d7fa2eb/LICENSE) contains disclosure and use restrictions, including restrictions on inferring personal attributes. We do not transfer this code to such applications. Native idea generation, literature search, agent-driven edits, full training, manuscript generation and automated review remain unexecuted. The isolated runner, full native reproduction, independent evaluation and publishing gates are tracked in [issue #797](https://github.com/Daisuke134/anicca-ops/issues/797).

The useful result is a limited experiment whose conditions and failures can be inspected, not a claim that the whole AI Scientist has been reproduced.
